parallel.requirements: Recognized the Rust 2021, std-only, CLI, Cargo project, test20.rs, and black-box binary requirements from the prompt, then decomposed behavior by inflection function families.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent performed initial probing, launched three parallel probe-only exploration children, waited for their reports, then assigned all implementation, build, and fuzz verification to a fourth coder child.
parallel.implementation: The coder child wrote Cargo.toml, test20.rs, inflection/mod.rs, and a Rust fuzz harness; it built successfully, found 195 titleize mismatches, fixed titleize to use space only, and removed the obsolete helper.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: Implementation writes went directly to the final /output workspace rather than via separate component merge, and artifact validation later copied the expected project and executable files.
parallel.verification: The child performed an initial successful build and a fuzz run that exposed the titleize issue; its final cargo build plus fuzz verification command was interrupted before a completed child report returned.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No final evaluator-visible functional defect remained because the official run passed 40/40, but the parallel process ended cancelled with no completed coder handoff after the final verification command.

serial.requirements: Recognized the same Rust 2021, std-only, CLI, Cargo project, root test20.rs, black-box inference, and byte-for-byte output requirements.
serial.plan_and_ownership: One main agent owned probing, implementation, file creation, bug fixing, build, differential testing, and final response without delegating to child agents.
serial.implementation: The serial agent wrote Cargo.toml, inflection/rules.rs, inflection/strings.rs, inflection/mod.rs, and test20.rs, then fixed tableize ordering and parameterize edge-dash stripping after differential tests.
serial.integration_and_delivery: The serial agent assembled the Cargo package itself, kept module contracts local, produced /output/test20.rs and executables, and listed the final project structure before completion.
serial.verification: Serial built with rustc and cargo, ran hand-picked probes, 946 fuzz cases, crash/no-arg/extra-arg checks, same-stderr checks, and a final regression with fail=0.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The serial trajectory ended normally after final verification and official evaluation passed 40/40; no unresolved process or implementation gap was visible at closure.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel recognized the same task obligations and broke them into behavior families for black-box probing before coding.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recognized the same obligations and explicitly summarized all inferred semantics before writing files.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No requirement coverage difference survived to evaluation; the contrast is that parallel externalized requirement discovery into child reports before implementation, while serial kept the requirements in one local thread.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel assigned three completed probe-only children and a later single implementation child, making implementation dependent on the investigation phase finishing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one owner for investigation, implementation, bug fixes, and acceptance checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel decomposition produced pseudo-concurrency: probe agents overlapped, but implementation was serialized after their reports. Serial used no children but kept the productive path continuously owned.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel parent received the three probe summaries and built a complete coder brief, but one titleize assumption in the implementation context was later contradicted by fuzzing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial carried probe findings directly into implementation and corrected mismatches locally as they appeared.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The parallel handoff did not leave an unresolved wrong artifact, because the coder detected and fixed the titleize issue; the concrete contrast is extra handoff and correction pressure, not an enduring context omission.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel implemented directly in one coder child after the reports, writing Cargo.toml, test20.rs, inflection/mod.rs, and a fuzz harness.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial implemented directly in the main agent, split library code into rules and strings modules, then edited those files after test mismatches.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both converged to passing behavior, but serial made and fixed its implementation defects inside one continuous loop, while parallel's single coder child had to absorb all implementation and late correction after the probe phase.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All three probe results returned to the parent, but the implementation child was stopped before a successful final handoff.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle and ended by producing a final completion message after verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel completed the investigation joins but failed the coder-child result lifecycle at the end; serial had no comparable handoff risk.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: The implementation child wrote the final project files in /output; there is no evidence of competing live implementation writers or overwrites.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: The serial main agent wrote and edited its own final project files without concurrent writers.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No shared-state collision explains any outcome difference. Parallel used a shared final workspace, but only the coder child owned the implementation writes.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel performed build and fuzz verification inside the coder child; after finding and fixing 195 titleize mismatches, its final verification command was interrupted.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial performed build checks, hand-picked comparisons, 946 fuzz cases, crash/no-arg checks, and final regression fail=0 before responding done.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both official evaluations passed, but serial had complete pre-closure acceptance evidence in the trajectory; parallel's last visible verification was interrupted, making the process adverse even though the artifact was valid.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed the run budget with a first investigation phase plus a late coder child, and the main and child turns were cancelled at the end.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial completed normally after 1577.182 agent seconds, with provider retry metadata showing remaining budget and prompt success.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel suffered closure pressure from phase ordering, while serial finished its final response and preserved explicit pre-closure verification evidence.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations show both artifacts passed all 40 test cases, so there is no discordant official outcome. The substantive difference is process-level: parallel timed out after a staged probe phase and an interrupted coder child, while serial completed a continuous local verification loop.
parallel_contributors: Parallel deferred implementation until after all probe children returned, then lost the coder child's final verification handoff to cancellation.
serial_contributors: Serial kept implementation and acceptance checks in one actor and completed a final regression with fail=0 before final response.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial initially misimplemented tableize order and parameterize edge stripping, then fixed both through differential tests.
Parallel initially carried a wrong titleize separator assumption into implementation, but the coder child found and fixed it before official evaluation.

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly delegated implementation to a coder child after the probe phase, so implementation had an owner even though that owner was later interrupted.
No separately owned component implementations required later interface reconciliation; the one coder child owned the final Rust project writes.
The coder child wrote Cargo.toml and test20.rs directly in /output, and artifact validation found the expected package and executable outputs.
The pipeline was assigned to the coder child as a complete implementation, build, fuzz, and report task; the problem was late staging, not absent pipeline ownership.
There was no single mandatory preflight harness or oracle blocking all work; the parent chose a broad completed investigation phase across three probe children.

Three investigation children overlapped only with each other, and the parent waited for their reports before assigning implementation to a later coder child, leaving that child to implement and verify under closure pressure.
candidates.realized_consequence: Implementation and final verification were compressed into the last phase, and the implementation child was stopped during its final build/fuzz command, leaving no completed child handoff to the parent even though the saved artifact later passed official evaluation.
candidates.near_match_reason: The fan-out itself was not excessive or retry-driven; the concrete adverse pattern is that productive implementation was delayed until after the probe phase.

candidates.reason: The indispensable implementation path started late, but that is the same serial-investigation chain and is not a separate capacity allocation episode.
The record shows three probe children and one coder child, not excessive breadth or repeated retries collectively consuming budget independent of the staged investigation.
The coder child had broad scope but produced the final project, corrected a mismatch, and left only final verification interrupted; scope overload is not independently proven.

The implementation brief carried the task and delivery requirements; the wrong titleize separator assumption was detected and fixed by the child, so no omitted known requirement made the work unusable.
No independently implemented components had to interoperate across child boundaries; probe outputs fed one final implementation owner.
The probe reports returned to the parent and were used to form the coder brief; no known finding is shown disappearing through transfer and causing repeated work.
Although the reports were substantial, the parent summarized and used them; the later issue was verification pressure, not failure to reduce an available handoff.
No child or parent acted on a report describing a superseded workspace or requirement state after a newer state was available.
No incompatible child reports remained unadjudicated at integration; the titleize mismatch was found against the reference and corrected by the coder child.
The parallel parent did not make an observable whole-task completion decision; the run was cancelled after a failed child handoff, and evaluator status is not used as retained evidence.
There was no retry or replacement agent that restarted without inherited findings; the three probe children and one coder child were first attempts for distinct scopes.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: The coder child was cancelled during final verification, but that is the terminal symptom of the retained serial-investigation chain; it is not retained as a second label for the same episode.
The final project files were already written in /output and accepted by artifact validation; there was no complete candidate left unpromoted or unplaced before closure.
The visible edits, including the titleize fix, occurred before the interrupted final verification command rather than after an accepted integrated verification.
The implementation child wrote directly to the final workspace, so there was no separate completed implementation artifact that the parent failed to retrieve or adopt.
No separate verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent; the interrupted work was the coder child's own final verification.
The parent received a failed stopped-child result only as the run itself was being cancelled, and this is not a distinct takeover episode separate from the late serial-investigation closure pressure.
The completed probe results were visible to the parent and explicitly consumed before implementation delegation; no available completed result was ignored.
The parent waited on an active coder child and then received the stopped-child result; there is no evidence of ignored available progress that would have changed the next action.
No concurrent agents wrote different implementation paths claiming overlapping behavior; the probe children were read-only and the coder child wrote the project.
No two live agents edited the same source or configuration file with one observing or reconciling the other's concurrent change.
No agent replaced, deleted, or wholesale rewrote non-entry source that another live agent had produced or actively owned.
The required entry point and executable were not overwritten by competing live owners; only the implementation child wrote the deliverable files.
There was no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion that replaced another agent's final-tree work or invalidated provenance.
The implementation used the shared /output workspace, but there is no concrete unstable-state or provenance problem from multiple live writers.
No generated file, fixture, cache, or auxiliary artifact from one parallel actor was consumed by another as reference input or stable environment state.

retained_patterns.reason: Parallel used concurrent children only for the investigation phase, then deferred implementation to one late coder child. The coder child had to correct a titleize mismatch and was interrupted during final build/fuzz verification, while the serial main agent completed final regression before ending.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Implementation and final verification were compressed into the last phase, and the implementation child was stopped during its final build/fuzz command, leaving no completed child handoff to the parent even though the saved artifact later passed official evaluation.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The fan-out itself was not excessive or retry-driven; the concrete adverse pattern is that productive implementation was delayed until after the probe phase.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Critical-Path Starvation, Early Child Termination, No Failure Takeover, and Blind Timeout Wait were considered but treated as downstream or alternate descriptions of the same late implementation closure chain.

Incomplete Child Brief and Conflicting Handoff were considered for the titleize mismatch, but the child detected and fixed the issue before official evaluation and no unresolved context conflict remained.
